name: Microsoft RDP
description: Microsoft's native remote desktop protocol, built into Windows since XP. Free with a Windows Pro/Enterprise or Server license — no separate app subscription, but multi-user Remote Desktop Services scenarios require paid RDS CALs.

Wayland Unattended Access.comment: Not a Windows feature; on Linux, GNOME's built-in Remote Desktop (mutter/FreeRDP-based) offers RDP over Wayland since GNOME 42

4:4:4 Chroma Subsampling.comment: RDP 10's AVC444 mode transmits full 4:4:4 chroma (as two 4:2:0 streams) for crisp text, unlike standard H.264

Frame Rate (FPS).comment: Capped at 30 FPS out of the box; reaching 60 FPS requires enabling AVC444 + hardware encoding via Group Policy

Session Recording.comment: Not native to RDP itself; requires third-party PAM tools (e.g. Secret Server) or RDS session recording features

ISO Mounting.comment: Local drives can be redirected into the session, but this isn't virtual media/ISO mounting like a KVM

Adaptive Bitrate.comment: RDP auto-detects bandwidth and adjusts graphics quality/compression accordingly

H.264 Codec.comment: RDP 10 uses AVC/H.264 as its primary graphics codec, with optional hardware encoding

H.265 Codec.comment: HEVC hardware encode/decode support depends on the GPU (e.g. modern Intel iGPUs); not universally enabled

Multi-User Sessions.comment: This is RDP's original defining feature — Remote Desktop Services/Terminal Services supports many isolated concurrent sessions

Tailscale Support.comment: No native integration; RDP just needs network reachability to port 3389, which Tailscale can provide

Open Source.comment: The protocol spec (MS-RDPBCGR) is openly published; Microsoft's own implementation is closed, but FreeRDP is an independent OSS client/server

Multi-Monitor Support.comment: Native support for spanning the session across multiple client monitors

Microphone Passthrough.comment: Audio redirection supports both playback and microphone recording from client to host

Wake-on-LAN.comment: RD Connection Broker/Gateway can wake VDI hosts via WoL in enterprise deployments; not built into plain point-to-point RDP

Pre-Login Access.comment: Defining feature — RDP itself is the Windows login screen, no separate pre-installed agent needed

No Account Required.comment: Just needs the target machine's local Windows account credentials, no Microsoft cloud account required

Shared Clipboard.comment: Bidirectional clipboard sync for text and files

Windows: Host.comment: Requires Windows Pro/Enterprise or Server; inbound RDP hosting is not available on Windows Home editions

Windows: Client.comment: Built-in Remote Desktop Connection (mstsc.exe) client on every Windows edition

macOS: Host.comment: No native RDP server for macOS

macOS: Client.comment: Microsoft Remote Desktop app for Mac

Linux X11: Host.comment: Via third-party xrdp, not an official Microsoft product

Linux Wayland: Host.comment: GNOME's built-in Remote Desktop feature (mutter + FreeRDP) supports RDP over Wayland since GNOME 42

Linux: Client.comment: FreeRDP-based clients such as Remmina are the common way to connect from Linux

Android: Client.comment: Microsoft Remote Desktop app for Android

iOS: Client.comment: Microsoft Remote Desktop app for iOS

Web Browser: Client.comment: Available via RD Web Access / Azure Virtual Desktop's HTML5 web client, not for plain point-to-point RDP

NVIDIA RTX 4090.comment: RDP is an enterprise/productivity protocol, not benchmarked as a GPU-tier game-streaming tool

Intel iGPU (QuickSync).comment: Relevant for hardware H.264/HEVC encoding, but no published comparative benchmark exists

Free Tier.comment: Single-session RDP is included free with Windows Pro/Enterprise; multi-user RDS needs paid CALs

Personal: Monthly.comment: Included with a Windows Pro/Enterprise license you already own; no separate subscription

Team / Business: Monthly.comment: Remote Desktop Services Client Access Licenses are sold per user or per device, not as a monthly app fee

Enterprise.status: Licensed per RDS CAL / Windows Server
Enterprise.comment: Bundled into Windows Server + RDS CAL licensing, or Azure Virtual Desktop/Windows 365 subscriptions
